one_sentence_caption: End-to-end methodological audit and reproducible benchmarking workflow spanning behavioral questionnaire audits (Module 1), multi-site neuroimaging benchmarks (Modules 2-3), and uncertainty-aware conformal triage (Module 4).

Feature ablation across 4 screening cohorts demonstrates that near-perfect accuracy (AUROC ~ 1.0) is driven entirely by label-leaking questionnaire items, with performance collapsing to chance on demographics alone (AUROC 0.447-0.580; Tautology Index raw 0.84-1.11).

Scanner generalization forest plot across 8 model architectures on ABIDE I (N=854, 20 sites), replacing the dense leaderboard table and illustrating consistent performance drops from random-CV (AUROC 0.672-0.771) to honest LOSO evaluation (AUROC 0.609-0.700).

Per-site LOSO AUROC forest plot with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and sample sizes across all 20 ABIDE I sites for primary logistic regression, compared against chance (0.50), site prevalence oracle (0.5902), and pooled LOSO AUROC (0.6593).

Controlled 20x20 site-decoding confusion matrix demonstrating that connectomes retain 73.54% site decodability (vs 19.91% majority baseline) even after strictly regressing out age, sex, FIQ, head motion, and diagnosis in training folds, representing broad site-associated information rather than hardware signatures alone.

Descriptive heatmap of mean CC200 functional connectivity differences (ASD minus Control, N=854) alongside heatmap of mean absolute logistic regression coefficients averaged across 20 LOSO training folds.

Within-site label permutation null distribution with B=10,000 resamples for primary LOSO logistic regression, showing observed AUROC of 0.6593 and empirical p = (1 + 0) / (1 + 10,000) = 0.00010 at the minimum resolution limit.

Grouped bar chart replacing the dense conformal table: empirical coverage at nominal 90% alongside prediction set decomposition (singleton vs triage referral) across tabular screening cohorts and ABIDE allocation protocols (Shared, Disjoint, Site-Grouped).

Systematic literature meta-audit across 33 peer-reviewed autism ML studies (2013-2026), documenting widespread feature leakage (93.8%), multi-site random cross-validation (77.4%), and near-complete neglect of probabilistic calibration and conformal uncertainty (93.9% reporting neither).
